1	Many liquid handling installations add a small, accurately measured quantity of a concentrate to a much larger stream of a carrier liquid that is already flowing in a pipe. The concentrate may be aggressive, staining, strongly colored, biologically active, or simply expensive, and the quantity that must be added is small in comparison with the carrier flow. The addition therefore has to be made repeatably, without measuring the concentrate by eye, and without allowing the concentrate to reach any part of the installation other than the carrier stream itself.
2	
3	Two practical difficulties dominate this kind of dosing. The first is separation of the two liquids upstream of the point of addition. Where a dosing device sits between a concentrate source and a carrier line under pressure, a path that momentarily connects the two can allow carrier liquid to be forced back toward the concentrate source, or can allow concentrate to reach the carrier line at a time when no dose is called for. Where the two sides are kept apart by separately actuated shut-off elements, the separation depends on those elements being commanded in the correct order.
4	
5	The second difficulty is residue. The surfaces that the concentrate touches, in particular the port through which it enters the metering volume and the seat of the check element through which the dose leaves, may retain a film of concentrate after the dose has been delivered. Where such a film passes into the carrier stream between doses, the quantity actually added is not the quantity that was measured; and where it dries or reacts on the wetted surfaces, the accuracy of the valve changes in service. Where the valve must be broken out of the line and cleaned by hand, the installation is taken out of service; and where a rinse is a separate operation commanded after the dose, it depends on that operation being performed at the right moment.
6	
7	Dose selection presents a further difficulty. Adjustable dosing devices may be set by a screw or by an electronically stored value. There remains a need for a setting that is retained by the mechanism itself and that is visible at the valve without electronics.
8	
9	There remains a need for an inline metering valve in which the separation of the concentrate from the carrier liquid is enforced by the geometry of the moving parts rather than by the order in which external commands arrive, in which the surfaces wetted by the concentrate are rinsed by the carrier liquid as an unavoidable part of the return of the metering element, and in which the selected dose is both retained and displayed mechanically.

The concentrate may be aggressive, staining, strongly colored, biologically active, or simply expensive, and the quantity that must be added is small in comparison with the carrier flow. The addition therefore has to be made repeatably, without measuring the concentrate by eye, and without allowing the concentrate to reach any part of the installation other than the carrier stream itself.

Two practical difficulties dominate this kind of dosing. The first is separation of the two liquids upstream of the point of addition. Where a dosing device sits between a concentrate source and a carrier line under pressure, a path that momentarily connects the two can allow carrier liquid to be forced back toward the concentrate source, or can allow concentrate to reach the carrier line at a time when no dose is called for. Where the two sides are kept apart by separately actuated shut-off elements, the separation depends on those elements being commanded in the correct order.

The second difficulty is residue. The surfaces that the concentrate touches, in particular the port through which it enters the metering volume and the seat of the check element through which the dose leaves, may retain a film of concentrate after the dose has been delivered. Where such a film passes into the carrier stream between doses, the quantity actually added is not the quantity that was measured; and where it dries or reacts on the wetted surfaces, the accuracy of the valve changes in service. Where the valve must be broken out of the line and cleaned by hand, the installation is taken out of service; and where a rinse is a separate operation commanded after the dose, it depends on that operation being performed at the right moment.

Dose selection presents a further difficulty. Adjustable dosing devices may be set by a screw or by an electronically stored value. There remains a need for a setting that is retained by the mechanism itself and that is visible at the valve without electronics.

There remains a need for an inline metering valve in which the separation of the concentrate from the carrier liquid is enforced by the geometry of the moving parts rather than by the order in which external commands arrive, in which the surfaces wetted by the concentrate are rinsed by the carrier liquid as an unavoidable part of the return of the metering element, and in which the selected dose is both retained and displayed mechanically.

input.summary:
SOURCE LEDGER — RESULT

I traced every claim limitation, every numbered part, and every structure, relationship, result, position, connection, operating condition and variant in draft/04 through draft/10, draft/numerals.md and the four figure briefs to the disclosure (input/disclosure.md) and the single USER passage in input/conversation.md (which is verbatim identical to the disclosure). The only other passage in the conversation is labeled YOU and was treated as context only; input/brief.md was used only for the title, "Not applicable." cross-reference and government-support statements, claim classes, means-plus-function instruction, and the preserved terminology list.

Traced and supported (no findings): cylindrical housing with inlet at one axial end and outlet at the opposite end (claim 12; desc. ¶2); metering sleeve fixed within the housing defining a cylindrical dose chamber, radial concentrate port, carrier-liquid admission port, and flush bypass opening downstream of the dose chamber; piston sliding between fill and discharge positions with two axially spaced sealing lands and a reduced-diameter waist; fill-position registration of the waist with the concentrate port and isolation of the carrier-liquid path by both lands; closure of the concentrate port before the downstream land uncovers the admission port; carrier liquid entering behind the measured volume and expelling it through the one-way outlet valve toward the outlet; the axial-ordering rule of claim 5 and desc. ¶9 (a tight consequence of "The ordering of the port edges and lands prevents the concentrate source from communicating directly with the carrier-liquid inlet"); the annular rinse channel between sleeve and housing; two radial rinse openings, one directed across the concentrate port and one across the one-way outlet valve (claims 2, 15); the flexible lip on the upstream sealing land wiping the dose-chamber wall first (claims 3, 14); the follower pin on the piston rod opening the normally closed flush poppet near the end of the return stroke and the poppet closing before the waist reconnects the concentrate port (claims 1, 4, 13, 16); the index collar surrounding the sleeve with a helical cam groove engaged by the follower pin and turned one increment per full stroke (claims 6, 17); three selectable axial stop faces setting three dose volumes by limiting piston travel (claims 7, 18); a spring-biased detent in one of three recesses (claims 8, 19); the transparent window showing one of three collar-carried dose setting numerals without electronics (claims 9, 19); the replaceable cartridge holding piston, sleeve, one-way outlet valve and flush poppet, retained by a threaded end cap whose removal withdraws the cartridge without disturbing the inlet and outlet connections (claims 10, 11, 20). All 29 numerals in draft/numerals.md are defined once, used consistently in the description, and assigned to exactly one part in each brief (18 = sleeve, 22 = concentrate port, 44 = follower pin on both of their sheets). The four figure-brief views match draft/07-drawings.md verbatim in view type, subject and piston state. No section line is designated in any view, so no cutting-plane designation is required or missing. No drafting note, placeholder, open question, instruction, unresolved alternative or internal comment survives in any file. No prior-art citation appears anywhere in the application, consistent with the empty prior_art/INDEX.md; the Background is uniformly conditional/need-framed and asserts no invention matter.

Depiction conventions reviewed and accepted: the schematic inlet/outlet stubs, the simple-outline transparent window panel, the plain closure elements for the one-way outlet valve and flush poppet, the blank patches standing for the dose setting numerals, the broken-line groove with hand and pitch expressly not indicated, the divided end face for the stop faces with the carrying end and the abutting part expressly not indicated, and the recess depth/profile and detent entry direction expressly not indicated. Each is confined to the figure brief, is labeled "shown schematically", and is not verbalized anywhere in draft/07 or draft/08; the description and claims remain shape-neutral, and no "by way of example" or "any outline" language was added to the application text to justify a renderer's choice. The FIG-1 and FIG-2/3 statements that the drawn axial end of the end cap, the radial position of the inlet, and the sleeve band in which each port is drawn are conventions only are likewise brief-confined and add no technical relationship.

FINDINGS (3): no disclosure-fidelity gap was found — every limitation, part, relationship and variant traces to an affirmative inventor passage. The defects are two figure-brief targeting inconsistencies in FIG. 3, where numerals 22 and 62 are identified purely by "leftmost" position while the brief's own geometry does not fix the axial order of the competing openings in the same sleeve band, and one facial text tension between the sleeve being "fixed within the housing" and being contained in a cartridge "removable from the housing as a unit". Each has a filing-clean automatic fix that adds no new matter.

findings.title: FIG. 3 target for numeral 22 (concentrate port) is identified only as "the leftmost upper opening", which the brief's own geometry assigns to the flush bypass passage
findings.where: figures/FIG-3.md, Targets list ("22: interior of the leftmost upper opening"), read against Geometry bullets 3, 5 and 6
findings.detail: FIG-3 describes three separate features entering or passing through the upper sleeve band: the concentrate port (bullet 5), the one-way outlet valve passage (bullet 6), and the flush bypass passage, which runs from a flush poppet placed "Adjacent the left end of the sleeve" "into the upper sleeve band toward the outlet end" (bullet 7). The poppet is at the extreme left because it is reached by the pin on the shaft that "extend[s] leftward past the sleeve's left end" near the end of the return stroke, whereas the concentrate port lies further right, clear of the sealing lands of a piston drawn "In the left half of the bore". The purely positional target "the leftmost upper opening" therefore does not uniquely identify the concentrate port and, on the brief's own stated left-to-right order, points at the flush bypass entry instead. Numeral 26 is separately targeted to "the interior of the bypass passage", so the two lead lines would land on the same feature. This makes numeral 22 mean two different parts across FIG. 2 (where it is targeted feature-wise to "the opening in the upper sleeve band above the waist") and FIG. 3.

findings.detail: FIG-3 places three openings in the lower sleeve band: the two rinse openings (bullet 8, "one adjacent the concentrate port and one adjacent the outlet-valve passage, each clear of the sealing lands") and the carrier-liquid admission port (bullet 9, "covered by the piston's right portion"). Because the piston is drawn "In the left half of the bore", the admission port is itself in the left half, while the brief never fixes the axial position of the concentrate port relative to the piston, saying only that its inner mouth is "clear of the sealing lands". If the concentrate port is drawn to the right of the piston, the leftmost lower opening is the admission port, and numeral 62 would label the unnumbered carrier-liquid admission port instead of a rinse opening. The target is therefore not uniquely determined by the brief and can contradict the detailed description, which uses 62 only for the radial rinse openings ("The two radial rinse openings 62 pass through the wall of the metering sleeve 18 and connect the annular rinse channel 60 to the dose chamber 20").

SOURCE LEDGER — RESULT

I traced every claim limitation, every numbered part, and every structure, relationship, result, position, connection, operating condition and variant in draft/04 through draft/10, draft/numerals.md and the four figure briefs to the disclosure (input/disclosure.md) and the single USER passage in input/conversation.md (verbatim identical to the disclosure). Traced and supported (no findings): cylindrical housing with inlet at one axial end and outlet at the opposite end (claim 12; desc. para 2); metering sleeve fixed within the housing defining a cylindrical dose chamber, radial concentrate port, carrier-liquid admission port and flush bypass opening downstream of the dose chamber; piston sliding between fill and discharge positions with two axially spaced sealing lands and a reduced-diameter waist; fill-position registration of the waist with the concentrate port and isolation of the carrier-liquid path by both lands; closure of the concentrate port before the downstream land uncovers the admission port; carrier liquid entering behind the measured volume and expelling it through the one-way outlet valve toward the outlet; the axial-ordering rule of claim 5 and desc. para 9 (a tight consequence of "The ordering of the port edges and lands prevents the concentrate source from communicating directly with the carrier-liquid inlet"); the annular rinse channel between sleeve and housing; two radial rinse openings, one directed across the concentrate port and one across the one-way outlet valve (claims 2, 15); the flexible lip on the upstream sealing land wiping the dose-chamber wall first (claims 3, 14); the follower pin on the piston rod opening the normally closed flush poppet near the end of the return stroke and the poppet closing before the waist reconnects the concentrate port (claims 1, 4, 13, 16); the index collar surrounding the sleeve with a helical cam groove engaged by the follower pin and turned one increment per full stroke (claims 6, 17); three selectable axial stop faces setting three dose volumes by limiting piston travel (claims 7, 18); a spring-biased detent in one of three recesses (claims 8, 19); the transparent window showing one of three collar-carried dose setting numerals without electronics (claims 9, 19); the replaceable cartridge holding piston, sleeve, one-way outlet valve and flush poppet, retained by a threaded end cap whose removal withdraws the cartridge without disturbing the inlet and outlet connections (claims 10, 11, 20). All 29 numerals in draft/numerals.md are defined once, used consistently in the description, and assigned to exactly one part per brief (18 = sleeve, 22 = concentrate port, 44 = follower pin on both of their sheets). The four figure-brief views match draft/07-drawings.md in view type, subject and piston state. No section line is designated in any view, so no cutting-plane designation is required or missing. No drafting note, placeholder, open question, instruction, unresolved alternative or internal comment survives in any file. No prior-art citation appears anywhere, consistent with the empty prior_art/INDEX.md; the Background is uniformly conditional/need-framed and asserts no invention matter.

Depiction conventions reviewed and accepted: the schematic inlet/outlet stubs, the simple-outline transparent window panel, the plain closure elements for the one-way outlet valve and flush poppet, the blank patches standing for the dose setting numerals, the broken-line groove with hand and pitch expressly not indicated, the divided end face for the stop faces with the carrying end and the abutting part expressly not indicated, and the recess depth/profile and detent entry direction expressly not indicated. Each is confined to the figure brief, is labeled "shown schematically", and is not verbalized in draft/07 or draft/08; the description and claims remain shape-neutral, and no "by way of example" or "any outline" language was added to the application text to justify a renderer's choice. The FIG-1 and FIG-2/3 statements that the drawn axial end of the end cap, the radial position of the inlet, and the sleeve band in which each port is drawn are conventions only are likewise brief-confined and add no technical relationship.

FINDINGS (3): no disclosure-fidelity gap was found; every limitation, part, relationship and variant traces to an affirmative inventor passage. The defects are two FIG. 3 targeting inconsistencies, where numerals 22 and 62 are identified purely by "leftmost" position while the brief's own geometry does not fix the axial order of the competing openings in the same sleeve band, and one facial text tension between the sleeve being "fixed within the housing" and being contained in a cartridge "removable from the housing as a unit". Each has a filing-clean fix that adds no new matter.

findings.title: FIG. 3 target for numeral 22 (concentrate port) is identified only as "the leftmost upper opening", which the brief's own geometry assigns to the flush bypass passage
findings.where: figures/FIG-3.md, Targets list ("22: interior of the leftmost upper opening"), read against Geometry bullets 5, 6 and 7
findings.detail: FIG-3 describes three separate features entering or passing through the upper sleeve band: the concentrate port, the one-way outlet valve passage, and the flush bypass passage, which runs from a flush poppet placed "Adjacent the left end of the sleeve" "into the upper sleeve band toward the outlet end". Compare figures/FIG-2.md, which targets 22 feature-wise: "- 22: interior of the opening in the upper sleeve band above the waist."
findings.fix: In figures/FIG-3.md, replace the target line "- 22: interior of the leftmost upper opening." with "- 22: interior of the opening through the upper sleeve band from which the broken-off concentrate stub rises, clear of the sealing lands."

findings.title: FIG. 3 target for numeral 62 (radial rinse opening) is identified only as "the leftmost lower opening", which the brief does not fix and which may be the carrier-liquid admission port
findings.where: figures/FIG-3.md, Targets list ("62: the leftmost lower opening"), read against Geometry bullets 3, 5, 8 and 9
findings.detail: FIG-3 places three openings in the lower sleeve band: the two rinse openings ("one adjacent the concentrate port and one adjacent the outlet-valve passage, each clear of the sealing lands") and the carrier-liquid admission port ("covered by the piston's right portion"). findings.fix: In figures/FIG-3.md, replace the target line "- 62: the leftmost lower opening." with "- 62: the opening through the lower sleeve band that lies beneath, and discharges across, the inner mouth of the concentrate port."
